Comment: The baseline planner has access to full V2X perception but yields 2.952 collisions per route. The paper never justifies why retraining the planner for safety is not the primary solution.
Revision: Added a paragraph in the Introduction justifying the frozen-adapter design over retraining the planner.

Comment: The 'collaborative' aspect is not ablated against a single-agent perception baseline.
Revision: Ran the no-collaboration ablation (105 routes); added result to Results.

Comment: The QP coefficients in Equations 11-13 lack a derivation from the continuous barrier derivative.
Revision: Added a derivation paragraph for the QP coefficients in Method; no code change.

Comment: Actor acceleration is silently ignored, which is highly problematic for modeling pedestrians and cyclists.
Revision: Added a worst-case actor-acceleration bound to the h_i equation in Method.

Comment: The direction alignment term eta_i disables the filter for lateral actors. For a 90-degree crossing, eta_i is approx 0, removing longitudinal protection exactly when it is needed for vulnerable road users.
Revision: Added an eta_floor guard to the alpha_i coefficient in Method.

Comment: Using a slack penalty (w_s = 1000) creates soft constraints, voiding the forward-invariance guarantee central to CBFs. The frequency of nonzero slack activation during evaluation is never reported, so the actual rate of barrier violations is unknown.
Revision: Measured slack-activation and solver-fallback rates; added to Results and a new Limitations paragraph.

Comment: Training and evaluation occur entirely on Town05. Generalization is not proven. (Also Q5: results on a held-out map?)
Revision: Ran zero-shot evaluation on Town07 and Town10; added to Results.

Comment: The evaluation checkpoint was improperly selected using the highest score on the test routes, artificially inflating the reported metrics.
Revision: Fixed the selection methodology in code; headline number not yet regenerated -- stated as a limitation.

Comment: The fixed CBF baseline (gamma = 0.5) lacks a sensitivity sweep, making the 25.9% improvement claim weak.
Revision: Ran the full 8-point gamma sweep; added table and figure to Results.

Comment: No ablations exist for major design choices: class-specific vs global gamma, observation space, cost function components, or PID vs simple Lagrangian.
Revision: Ran training-free proxies for two (class-specific-gamma, observation-space); the other two (cost-function, PID-Lagrangian) not addressed, stated as future work.

Comment: The primary 'CARLA driving score' metric (reported as 75.81) is not mathematically defined regarding infraction weights.
Revision: Added the exact formula and infraction weights to Setup.

Comment: Critical cost parameters d_warn, d_col, tau_ttc are never assigned numerical values in the text or tables.
Revision: Added numeric values inline in Method.

Comment: Execution time is omitted. A proposed 5 Hz real-time safety system must document OSQP solve times in dense traffic.
Revision: Measured OSQP solve time; added to Results.

Comment: W1. Novelty is somewhat incremental; the main contribution is system integration/application rather than a fundamentally new method.
Revision: Expanded the Related Work comparison against Berducci et al.

Comment: W2. Experimental validation is too narrow for the strength of the claims: only Town05, one simulator setting, one upstream stack. (Also Q3: generalize under different traffic densities or scenario distributions?)
Revision: Added Town07/Town10 generalization and a traffic-density probe; simulator/stack diversity not addressed.

Comment: W3. The key fixed-CBF baseline is a single hand-tuned gain; no sweep or Pareto comparison is shown, so it is unclear whether adaptive scheduling truly outperforms the best static setting.
Revision: Same gamma sweep as Reviewer 1's item.

Comment: W4. Limited ablations: no comparison to a single adaptive gain, rule-based scheduler, or sensitivity to feature design and cost terms.
Revision: Ran the rule-based scheduler baseline; used the same proxies as Reviewer 1 for shared-gain/observation-space; cost-term sensitivity not addressed.

Comment: W5. Safety claims should be phrased carefully since the QP includes slack and solver fallback to the nominal command, which weakens formal guarantees.
Revision: Same slack/fallback measurements as Reviewer 1's item.

Comment: W6. The method only adjusts longitudinal control, which limits practical impact in many urban interaction cases.
Revision: Stated as a limitation in the Conclusion; not addressed.

Comment: Q2. How many training seeds were used, and how variable are the final results across seeds?
Revision: Not addressed; stated as future work.

Comment: Q6. How robust is the method to noise or latency in collaborative perception or V2X inputs?
Revision: Ran latency and pose-noise probes; added to Results.
